title: Best Claims Management Software for Insurers Compared (2026)
summary: Compare 12 claims management systems for carriers, MGAs, and TPAs: core suites, claims platforms, and AI layers, with integration and AI notes.
body_markdown:
**Claims management software is the system of record where an insurer opens, reserves, pays, and closes claims.** It comes in three types: core claims suites (Duck Creek Claims, Guidewire ClaimCenter, Majesco, Sapiens), configurable claims platforms (Origami Risk, Riskonnect, Snapsheet), and AI document and workflow layers that may sit on top of either (CLARA Analytics, Cytora, FurtherAI, Gradient AI, Verisk ClaimSearch). We recommend choosing the system of record first, based on your lines, volume, and integration needs, then adding an AI layer where documents and manual intake slow your adjusters down.


In this guide, we compare 12 options in one table, with an unranked profile of each, a decision list for core suite versus AI layer, and the questions to ask before you sign. It's written for claims and IT leaders at carriers, managing general agents (MGAs), and third-party administrators (TPAs) building a shortlist.


## **Key takeaways**


- **Pick the system of record and the AI layer separately.** Core suites and claims platforms hold the claim file, reserves, and payments. AI layers read documents and move data into that file, so they don't replace it.
- **Every core vendor now ships its own AI.** Guidewire, Duck Creek, Majesco, Riskonnect, Origami Risk, and Snapsheet all announced agentic or generative AI features in 2026, though some are early access.
- **Write-back is the integration test that matters.** Ask whether a tool can write structured results into your claims system with an audit trail, not just read from it.
- **Pilot in shadow mode.** Run the new tool beside your team, set an agreement threshold before go-live, and keep a person on every coverage and payment decision.


## **What does claims management software do?**


Claims management software runs the claim lifecycle from first notice of loss (FNOL) to closure. Most systems cover the same core jobs:


1. **Intake:** capture the loss through portals, email, phone, or an agent, and open the claim.
2. **Coverage verification:** match the claim to the policy and confirm what's covered.
3. **Assignment:** route the claim to an adjuster or queue by complexity, line, and workload.
4. **Reserving:** set and adjust reserves as facts develop.
5. **Payments:** issue indemnity and expense payments, including recurring and multi-payee payments.
6. **Correspondence:** send letters, requests, and status updates to claimants, brokers, and vendors.
7. **Reporting:** track cycle time, severity, leakage, and adjuster workload.
8. **Audit trail:** record who did what, when, and why.


Once AI enters the workflow, the audit trail needs one more layer. **Auditability means you can show the data the system used, what the model saw, and the decision a person made.** If a vendor can't show all three for a given claim, a market conduct examiner will have a hard time following the file.


## **Three types of claims platform**


**Core claims suites.** Enterprise systems of record for property and casualty (P&C) claims, usually sold alongside the same vendor's policy and billing systems. They hold the claim file, reserves, payments, and financial controls. Examples: Duck Creek Claims, Guidewire ClaimCenter, Majesco Intelligent Claims for P&C, and Sapiens ClaimsPro.


‍ **Claims platforms and point solutions.** Configurable claims administration systems, often cloud-native, that serve carriers, MGAs, TPAs, and self-insured organizations. Some are also risk management information systems (RMIS), and some started as point solutions for intake, estimating, or subrogation. Examples: Origami Risk, Riskonnect, and Snapsheet.


‍ **AI document and workflow layers.** Tools that sit on top of the system of record, read unstructured documents, score or route claims, and write results back. They don't hold the official claim file. Examples: CLARA Analytics, Cytora, FurtherAI, Gradient AI, and Verisk ClaimSearch (a data service).


If you're comparing tools that automate work around these systems, such as RPA, workflow builders, and no-code apps, see our guide to[choosing a claims automation vendor](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/claims-automation-software-selection) . For a ranked list of AI tools only, see the[best AI tools for insurance claims processing](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/best-ai-tools-insurance-claims-processing) .


## **How we evaluated claims management software**


We compared each vendor on six criteria:


1. **Fit** by line of business and by carrier, MGA, or TPA size
2. **Integration** and API availability, including write-back to the system of record
3. **Document intelligence and intake**
4. **Audit trail and explainability**
5. **Implementation effort** , described qualitatively and only where a source states it
6. **Pricing model** , limited to what's published


Sources are public vendor pages, press releases, trade press, and analyst directories, reviewed on November 24, 2026. "Documented" means we found it in a public source. "Not documented" means we didn't, and it doesn't mean the capability doesn't exist. There are no scores or rankings, and vendors are listed alphabetically within each type. FurtherAI publishes this guide and is included as one entry, using the same format as every other vendor.

## **Vendor profiles by type**


### Core claims suites


#### Duck Creek Claims


Duck Creek launched an insurance-native agentic AI platform in April 2026 with an Agentic FNOL application, developed with Google Cloud on Gemini models, that adds policy and coverage verification and early fraud detection at intake, as per[Insurance-Canada](https://insurance-canada.ca/2026/04/30/duck-creek-launch-native-agentic-ai-platform/) .


- **Best for:** P&C carriers standardizing on Duck Creek for policy, billing, and claims.
- **Strengths:** AI built into the core suite, with governance and traceability for agent actions.
- **Limitations:** Agentic FNOL has been in early access since September 28, 2026, per our[FNOL automation platform comparison](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/top-fnol-automation-platforms-comparison) .
- **Integration:** An AI Gateway with a marketplace, registry, and MCP and A2A protocols for partner and customer-built agents.
- **Pricing model (as publicly stated):** Not published.


#### Guidewire ClaimCenter


ClaimCenter is Guidewire's claims system of record. At its Connections conference on October 27, 2026, Guidewire announced agents built into ClaimCenter that capture the loss, summarize the file, and flag risk, plus Concierge, which takes loss details by voice or chat, according to[Guidewire's announcement](https://finviz.com/news/408788/guidewire-delivers-the-open-secure-and-complete-core-platform-for-agentic-insurance) .


- **Best for:** Large, multi-line P&C carriers that want claims, policy, and billing from one vendor.
- **Strengths:** Functional depth, a large partner marketplace, and the ProNavigator adjuster assistant.
- **Limitations:** Some features announced in 2026 are early access or roadmap, as per[IT Brief](https://itbrief.com.au/story/guidewire-launches-agentic-ai-platform-for-insurers) .
- **Integration:** Guidewire Marketplace apps and partner accelerators run inside ClaimCenter, including integrations from CLARA Analytics and Verisk.
- **Pricing model (as publicly stated):** Not published.


#### Majesco Intelligent Claims for P&C


[Majesco describes its claims system](https://coverager.com/kyber-and-majesco-partner-to-automate-and-govern-claims-correspondence-in-majesco-intelligent-claims-for-pc/) as running FNOL through closure on one platform, with GenAI and agentic AI inside adjuster workflows.[Celent named it](https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260819594000/en/Majesco-Intelligent-Claims-for-PC-Recognized-as-a-Luminary-and-Earned-an-XCelent-Award-for-Breadth-of-Functionality-in-Celent-PC-Claims-Systems-North-America-Edition-Report) a Luminary in its 2026 P&C claims systems report.


- **Best for:** Mid-sized P&C carriers, such as Celina Insurance Group, moving to a cloud-native suite, according to[Business Wire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250128590732/en) .
- **Strengths:** Two-way email in claims and partner integrations including OFAC and LexisNexis.
- **Limitations:** Customer outcomes from its claims agents aren't documented publicly.
- **Integration:** Bi-directional integration with Kyber for claims correspondence, plus partner data services.
- **Pricing model (as publicly stated):** Not published.


#### Sapiens ClaimsPro


ClaimsPro is part of Sapiens CoreSuite for P&C and can also be deployed standalone, as per[Celent](https://www.celent.com/en/directory/companies/sapiens/solutions/908170297) . A state-run auto insurance placement and claims organization chose it to replace a decade-old system, according to[Financial IT](https://financialit.net/news/insurtech/leading-us-auto-claims-organization-selects-sapiens-modernize-operations) .


- **Best for:** P&C and workers' comp carriers already on Sapiens policy and billing.
- **Strengths:** Case management for complex, fraud, and litigated claims, plus catastrophe event handling, as per[Sapiens](https://sapiens.com/us/property-and-casualty/claimspro/) .
- **Limitations:** Specific 2026 claims-AI capabilities aren't documented publicly.
- **Integration:** Shares data across quotes, policies, claims, and accounts within CoreSuite.
- **Pricing model (as publicly stated):** Not published.


### Claims platforms and point solutions


#### Origami Risk


Origami Risk runs policy, billing, and claims administration on one cloud-native platform.[Tokio Marine HCC Specialty Group selected the full suite](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260414005399/en/) in April 2026 after a live proof of concept, and WCF Insurance chose its claims platform in July 2026, as stated in[Business Wire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729615995/en/) .


- **Best for:** Carriers, MGAs, TPAs, and risk pools that want one configurable platform.
- **Strengths:** Configuration flexibility across lines, plus client-facing portals for TPAs.
- **Limitations:** Its AI features, including a drag-and-drop AI Tile released in Q2 2026, are newer than its core claims administration, as per[Origami Risk](https://www.origamirisk.com/?p=21063) .
- **Integration:** Policy, billing, claims, and reporting share one data model.
- **Pricing model (as publicly stated):** Not published.


#### Riskonnect


[Riskonnect's claims management software](https://riskonnect.com/claims-management-software/) covers intake through settlement, including FROI and SROI injury filings, reserves, subrogation, and return to work. It serves carriers, TPAs, MGAs, and self-insured organizations.


- **Best for:** TPAs and self-insured organizations that want claims administration inside a wider RMIS.
- **Strengths:** Predictive models for litigation, subrogation, and claim duration, plus AI document summarization.
- **Limitations:** The claims page doesn't state a deployment model. Its Intelligent Risk Framework, announced in February 2026, is powered by Salesforce's Agentforce 360, as per[Tech Intel Pro](https://techintelpro.com/news/cybersecurity/risk-and-compliance/riskonnect-launches-enterprise-ai-for-risk-with-agentforce-360) , which IT teams should factor into architecture reviews.
- **Integration:** APIs and data transformation from more than 900 external carrier and TPA systems.
- **Pricing model (as publicly stated):** Depends on project size, complexity, and customization, with three implementation options.


#### **Snapsheet**


[Snapsheet](https://www.snapsheetclaims.com/post/snapsheet-named-a-luminary-in-celents-2026-north-america-p-c-claims-systems-report) is a cloud-native claims management platform. More than 75 P&C carriers, TPAs, MGAs, and logistics companies run claims on it, and it launched Snapsheet AI in July 2026.


- **Best for:** P&C carriers and MGAs replacing a legacy claims system on a defined timeline.
- **Strengths:** No-code workflows, built-in payments, and virtual appraisal roots.
- **Limitations:** Snapsheet AI is new, so documented customer outcomes for it are limited.
- **Integration:** APIs and a partner ecosystem;[Snapsheet says](https://www.snapsheetclaims.com/insurance-claims-management-software) implementation can take as little as 16 weeks.
- **Pricing model (as publicly stated):** Not published.


### AI document and workflow layers


#### CLARA Analytics


CLARA provides AI for casualty and workers' comp claims. In September 2026 it launched Agentic Intelligence, which puts AI agents on every claim from FNOL to resolution while adjusters keep control of decisions, as per[Claims Journal](https://www.claimsjournal.com/news/national/2026/09/29/340380.htm) .


- **Best for:** Casualty writers and TPAs managing severity, litigation, and medical costs.
- **Strengths:** A decade of casualty claims outcome data behind its models.
- **Limitations:** Focused on bodily injury lines; it doesn't serve as a claims system of record.
- **Integration:** CLARA insights appear inside Guidewire ClaimCenter, with claim data syncing automatically, according to[FinTech Futures](https://fintechfutures.com/?p=15344642) .
- **Pricing model (as publicly stated):** AI as a service; prices not published.


#### Cytora (Applied Systems)


Applied Systems acquired Cytora in September 2025. Applied describes it as a configurable platform that digitizes intake "from submission to claims servicing," as mentioned in[GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/09/09/3147130/27604/en/Applied-Systems-Acquires-Cytora.html) .


- **Best for:** Commercial carriers digitizing broker and email intake.
- **Strengths:** Agentic email-to-quote,[launched in August 2026](https://www1.appliedsystems.com/en-us/news/press-releases/2026/applied-launches-new-agentic-email-to-quote-submission-channel/) .
- **Limitations:** Its claims use cases are documented only at a high level; most published work is underwriting intake.
- **Integration:** Feeds existing policy administration, rating, and workflow systems.
- **Pricing model (as publicly stated):** Not published.


#### FurtherAI


FurtherAI is an insurance-native AI workspace that sits alongside the claims system of record, reads claim documents, and writes structured results back to it. Your policy administration and claims systems stay the systems of record.


- **Best for:** Commercial and specialty carriers, MGAs, and TPAs with high volumes of claim documents. It isn't built for very small agencies or personal-lines direct-to-consumer teams.
- **Strengths:** Source-linked findings, rationales, reviewer sign-off, human checkpoints, and logged agent and human actions. In one vendor-reported, deployment-specific case,[a specialty insurer automated more than 90% of claims intake](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/claims-processing-ai) and processed claims more than 10x faster.
- **Limitations:** It isn't a claims system of record. Published claims proof centers on intake and document work.
- **Integration:**[Native connectors](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/furtherai-launches-connectors-one-workspace-every-insurance-system) for Guidewire, Duck Creek, and Majesco,[agents that run inside PolicyCenter and ClaimCenter](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/furtherai-partners-with-guidewire-to-close-a-long-standing-gap-in-insurance-ai) , more than 100 enterprise integrations, and[Computer Use 2.0](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/introducing-computer-use-2-0-on-furtherai) (September 2026) for legacy screens without an API. The FurtherAI Accelerator for PolicyCenter is live on the[Guidewire Marketplace](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/furtherai-accelerator-guidewire-policycenter) , and FurtherAI has been available in the[Microsoft Marketplace](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/furtherai-now-available-in-the-microsoft-marketplace) since August 18, 2026.
- **Pricing model (as publicly stated):** Custom enterprise pricing.


#### Gradient AI


[Gradient AI](https://www.gradientai.com/press-gradient-ai-workers-comp-insurance-triage-solution/) builds predictive models for workers' comp, group health, and P&C. In March 2026 it launched ClaimVoyant, which flags potentially expensive or complex workers' comp claims at FNOL.


- **Best for:** Workers' comp carriers, TPAs, and self-insured groups.
- **Strengths:** An industry data lake of tens of millions of policies and claims. The MEMIC Group reported better reserving accuracy with Gradient's total incurred prediction model, as per[Business Wire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260512708503/en/)) .
- **Limitations:** Its claims triage is documented for workers' comp only.
- **Integration:** Designed to fit existing claims handling workflows.
- **Pricing model (as publicly stated):** Not published.


#### Verisk ClaimSearch


ClaimSearch is a data service, not a claims management system. It's a contributory database of more than 1.8 billion U.S. claims, representing about 95% of the U.S. P&C market, that claims and special investigations unit (SIU) teams check against, as per[Verisk](https://integration.verisk.com/blog/verisk-claimsearch-the-backbone-of-the-pc-claims-ecosystem/) .


- **Best for:** Claims and SIU teams checking claimants and losses against industry data.
- **Strengths:** Industry-wide matching, claim scoring, and image forensics.
- **Limitations:** It doesn't manage the claim lifecycle; you still need a system of record.
- **Integration:**[A Guidewire Marketplace Accelerator](https://www.verisk.com/blog/digital-media-forensics-joins-the-guidewire-marketplace/) puts Digital Media Forensics results inside ClaimCenter
- **Pricing model (as publicly stated):** Not published.


## **Core suite or AI layer: how to decide**


Most carriers end up with both: a system of record and at least one AI layer. The order matters, and these four questions settle it.


1. **Does your current claims or policy system have usable APIs?** If it does, an AI layer can read and write through them, and you can delay a core replacement. If it doesn't, check whether the AI layer can work through the screen, as computer use agents do, before you assume you need a new core.
2. **Where is the bottleneck: the system or the documents?** If adjusters lose time to claim notices, medical records, invoices, and loss runs, an AI layer addresses that faster than a new core. If reserves, payments, or financial controls are breaking, the system of record is the problem.
3. **How many lines, and how different?** Multi-line carriers with complex financials tend to need a core suite. Single-line or program-focused MGAs and TPAs often fit a configurable claims platform.
4. **What's your timeline?** Core replacements take long enough to need a multi-phase plan. An AI layer can usually start with one workflow and expand once it proves accuracy, so you can run it during a core migration and keep it afterward.


For how the layers connect, see our guide to[building an insurance AI stack for underwriting and claims](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/ai-platforms-insurance-claims-underwriting) .


## **How to evaluate and pilot claims software**


1. **Test on your own files.** Ask each finalist to process a sample of your closed claims, including your messiest documents.
2. **Run in shadow mode.** Let the new tool work beside your team and write its output to a hidden field, so it doesn't affect live decisions.
3. **Set an agreement threshold before go-live.** Decide how closely the tool must match your team's work before you switch it on, and how you'll measure that.
4. **Keep human review checkpoints.** A person approves coverage, reserve, and payment decisions, and the system logs who approved what.
5. **Expand one workflow at a time.** Measure cycle time and touch time before and after each step.


One publicly reported example:[Upland Specialty ran FurtherAI](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/upland-specialty-proved-furtherai-in-production-then-cut-clearance-time) in shadow mode on its clearance desk, comparing extractions with its team's manual work, and switched it on once agreement cleared 85%. That's a vendor-reported underwriting clearance deployment rather than a claims benchmark, but the same pattern applies to claims intake. Our guide on[deploying AI in production](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/how-to-deploy-ai-in-production-for-insurance) walks through it.


Read customer announcements carefully, ours included. An announcement doesn't prove that a deployment is still live, in scope, or renewed, and a named customer doesn't prove the tool fits your book, systems, or data.


## **Compliance and governance questions to ask vendors**


[The NAIC Model Bulletin on the Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems](https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/legal-adoption-map-ai-model-bulletin.pdf) by Insurers expects insurers to govern AI systems they buy from third parties as well as those they build. Put these questions in every RFP:


1. **Explainability:** Can a reviewer see the reasoning behind each recommendation and the source document it came from?
2. **Audit logs:** Does the system record the data used, what the model saw, and the human decision, and can you export that log for an exam?
3. **Human checkpoints:** Which actions can the system take on its own, and which need sign-off?
4. **Data handling:** Where is data stored, who can access it, and is it used to train models? Get the answer in the contract.
5. **Deployment:** Can the tool run in your own cloud or on dedicated infrastructure?
6. **Write-back:** Which fields does the tool write into your system of record, and how are errors caught?


For reference, FurtherAI runs each customer on dedicated, single-tenant infrastructure. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest, customers can manage their own encryption keys, and[FurtherAI contractually guarantees](https://www.furtherai.com/security) that customer data is never used to train, fine-tune, or improve any underlying models.

## **Frequently asked questions**


#### What is claims management software?


Claims management software is the system insurers, MGAs, and TPAs use to run a claim from first notice of loss to closure. It handles intake, coverage verification, assignment, reserving, payments, correspondence, and reporting, and it keeps the audit trail. Core suites such as Guidewire ClaimCenter and claims platforms such as Snapsheet are examples. AI tools usually sit on top of it rather than replacing it.


#### What is the difference between a claims core system and an AI claims layer?


A claims core system is the system of record: it holds the claim file, reserves, payments, and financial controls. An AI claims layer reads unstructured documents, extracts and checks data, and routes or scores claims, then writes results back to the core system. You need a core system to run claims. An AI layer reduces the manual document work around it.


#### Can AI work alongside Guidewire or Duck Creek without replacing them?


Yes. AI layers connect through APIs, marketplace integrations, or connectors and write results back into the claim file. FurtherAI, for example, has native connectors for Guidewire, Duck Creek, and Majesco and runs agents inside ClaimCenter, while CLARA Analytics shows its insights inside ClaimCenter. Guidewire and Duck Creek also ship their own AI features, so compare both routes.


#### What should a TPA look for in claims software?


A TPA should look for multi-client configuration, so one system can run several clients' books to different rules, plus client reporting portals and strong audit trails. Check workers' comp support if you handle it, including FROI and SROI filings. Riskonnect and Origami Risk both serve TPAs. Our guide to[AI for TPA claims processing](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/best-ai-claims-processing-and-adjudication-tpas) covers TPA-specific options in more depth.


#### How long does claims software implementation take?


It depends on the type. Replacing a core claims system is a multi-phase program that usually spans data migration, configuration, integration, and testing across lines of business. Configurable claims platforms tend to move faster, especially for a single line or program. An AI layer can usually start with one workflow, such as claims intake, and expand once it proves accuracy on your files.


#### How do I audit claims for leakage without sampling?


Use software that reviews every open and closed file against your coverage terms, reserve rules, and payment controls, rather than pulling a small sample. AI document tools can read the whole file, flag exceptions, and link each flag to its source so an auditor can confirm it. Treat leakage auditing as separate from fraud detection. Our guide to[claims leakage and fraud detection software](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/claims-leakage-fraud-detection-software-for-carriers) compares the options.


#### What integration questions should I ask vendors?


Ask whether the tool reads only or also writes back to your claims system, and which fields it writes. Ask which integration route it uses for your system (native connector, API, marketplace app, screen automation, or file exchange), and who maintains it through upgrades. Ask how errors are caught and logged. Then confirm each answer in a pilot on your own environment.


#### Does claims software include fraud detection?


Many claims systems include basic fraud indicators, and Duck Creek's Agentic FNOL adds early fraud detection at intake. Organized-fraud scoring and SIU case management are usually handled by specialists such as Shift Technology and FRISS, with industry data from services like Verisk ClaimSearch. Keep fraud scoring separate from leakage and overpayment auditing, since the two need different tools and owners. See our[FNOL automation platform comparison](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/top-fnol-automation-platforms-comparison) for intake-stage checks.
